To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DOC is the primary hormone that regulates the renin-aldosterone axis, (2) DOC is the major hormone that regulates the sodium balance, (3) DOC is the main hormone that regulates the potassium balance, and (4) DOC is the most important hormone that controls the blood pressure.

We have shown that the mineralocorticoids, aldosterone and deoxycorticoster- one (DOC), can have opposite effects on the regulation of the renin system, with aldosterone stimulating renin production and DOC suppressing renin production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pathophysiology of essential hypertension and with the identification of the factors responsible for the development of hypertension.
the study of a group of patients with essential hypertension and normal plasma aldosterone concentration.

the possible role of raised plasma-deoxycorticoster-one (DOC) levels as a factor in the pathogenesis and in the suppression-of renin secretion in a subgroup of patients with hypertension and normal aldosterone secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plasma-deoxycorticostero ne concentration is elevated in a significant proportion of patients with essential hypertension and that the DOC excess is associated with a low plasma renin level and with intermittent hypokalaemia.

the plasma-DOC concentration was persistently increased in six patients with low plasma- renin concentration and that the DOC concentration was intermittently raised in five further cases with low renin values.
the DOC excess syndrome is a rare cause of hypertension and that the syndrome is not necessarily associated with hypokalaemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DOC may be a cause of hypertension and hypokalaemia.

in the absence of aldosterone excess, the presence of a high DOC level is a useful marker for the presence of hypertension and that the presence of high DOC levels may indicate a need to search for a cause of hypertension other than primary aldosteronism.
in some cases of essential hypertension the renin-aldosterone system is inappropriately suppressed and that this is due to a circulating factor which is not DOC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mineralocorticoids are important in hypertension and the renin- angiotensin system can be suppressed by the mineralocorticosteroids.

the use of the renin assay to guide therapy in patients with primary aldosteronism is not a good idea, and that the use of a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone, eplerenone) is a better choice.
we have a better understanding of the role that the adrenal gland plays in the development of high blood pressure.
